title.narrative: "Integrated Support for Children in Drought-Affected Malawi: Enhancing Education, Nutrition, and WASH Services for Resilience and Well-being" (CERF UF)

description.narrative: The Nutrition component focuses on the early identification and referral of children with wasting and nutritional oedema. Children with moderate wasting without medical complications will be managed at the community level through Thanzi sessions, while those with severe wasting will be managed at health facilities in Nsanje, Chikwawa, Zomba and Machinga districts. Thanzi sessions are grounded in the 2023 WHO guidelines for preventing and managing wasting in children, which emphasize using locally available nutritious foods to manage moderate wasting. The project will target 240 Community-Based Childcare Centers (CBCCs) in Nsanje and 260 CBCCs in Chikwawa, along with surrounding communities. The project plans to reach 256,322 (up from the initially planned 127,779) children aged 6–59 months. Secondary beneficiaries will include 12,000 community leaders, faith leaders, and caregivers of children within this age group. UNICEF had initially intended to implement the activities through Farmers Union of Malawi as a partner. However, UNICEF will now implement the activities through Malawi Red Cross Society with whom we have an existing agreement for implementing similar activities in the same districts. This will enhance continuity and synergy in project activities.Under WASH, the original strategy was to implement directly through district councils, but capacity constraints —such as staffing shortages, logistical challenges, and reporting delays—have slowed implementation and now threaten the achievement of project targets within the agreed timeframe. UNICEF proposes engaging DCT to ensure timely, high-quality delivery of interventions while coordinating with district authorities. DCT is a trusted partner with a strong track record in risk communication and behaviour change, currently implementing education interventions under the same project.
